title: A wrong entry shows a message beside the field
note: Invalid fields show an inline message saying what to change; the form keeps what was typed.
intent: Rejecting a form silently, or with a red border alone, leaves the person guessing. Validate on submit (and on blur once a field has been touched), keep everything they typed, put a message directly under the field saying what to change in plain words ("Enter an email like name@example.com"), mark the field aria-invalid and connect the message with aria-describedby, and move focus to the first invalid field. Disable the submit button only while sending, never as the way to say the form is wrong. Declare a view named `invalid` that submits the form with bad values so the critic can photograph the state.

check.ask: Does every invalid field show a message next to it that says in words what to change, while keeping what was typed?
check.note: The view `invalid` submits the form wrongly: each bad field shows a specific inline message.

port: The form helper that emits label + input also emits an error slot; validation fills the slot and sets aria-invalid, so no facet writes its own error markup.
